cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: I Started the Weirdness
cards.instruction: Hide that one casual choice caused the impossible situation while eagerly helping manage each new consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I read my mug aloud like you. Cheers. Now the little demon's chewing our cookbook; rescue the book while I fetch food.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was reading a teabag label. Yours was a summoning spell.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Labels read, yes. Those novelty mugs say all sorts. I'll fetch crackers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only eats words. It's swallowed a recipe and it's heading for the lease.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give it my mug. You save the lease; let it chew the writing right off.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies reading as a toast; B2 identifies the spell, and A3 dismisses its importance while A5 helpfully removes its writing. Both concealment and uncomprehending confidence affect the rescue.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 makes A3 minimise the mug; B4's word diet turns A5's own causal object into the alternative food. Cookbook in A1 prepares the diet.

relationship.evidence: B2 knows what was read and B4 wants to protect the lease; A5 splits useful rescue work instead of arguing about blame.

heightening.evidence: A5 sacrifices the mug because B4 says words are food: the generous remedy destroys the incriminating writing as well.

specificity.evidence: A1 now explicitly asks B to rescue the book, not hold an ambiguous 'it'; B4's lease raises the immediate loss.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's casual novelty-mug dismissal and A5's practical offer carry concealment without an explanatory closing slogan.
